evals.name: saboteur-heavy-cache
evals.prompt:
Run an adversarial review on this file. It is new code added to a production codebase.

File: cache.ts

Produce the full adversarial-reviewer output (all three personas, final verdict).
evals.expected_output: BLOCK verdict. Saboteur finds: (1) null dereference in get() when key is missing (entry.expiresAt accessed before nullcheck), (2) get() returns entry.value after deleting expired entry — returns stale or undefined, (3) race condition in getOrLoad (thundering herd on concurrent misses), (4) no TTL validation allowing negative/zero TTL, (5) memory leak (expired entries never swept unless accessed). New Hire finds: thin names, no tests, no docstring. Security Auditor: cache poisoning risk, invalidate() pattern match is unescaped. Cross-promotion expected on missing tests and input validation.

assertions.text: Report flags null dereference in get() when key is missing
Report flags race condition / thundering herd in getOrLoad
Report flags memory leak from expired entries never being swept
Report includes all three persona sections (Saboteur, New Hire, Security Auditor)
Final verdict is BLOCK (has at least one CRITICAL finding)

evals.name: new-hire-heavy-process
evals.prompt:
Run an adversarial review on this file. It was just added to a reporting pipeline.

File: process.py

Produce the full adversarial-reviewer output (all three personas, final verdict).
evals.expected_output: CONCERNS or BLOCK verdict. New Hire dominates: function name `process` is meaningless, `mode=1` and `mode=2` are magic numbers, positional indexing `x[0]`..`x[4]` with no documented schema, magic numbers 1.08 / 1.15 / 0.95 / 90 / 30 unexplained, function violates SRP by both transforming data and writing a file. Saboteur: no input validation on src file, file write path is timestamp-based (could collide on concurrent runs), float() could throw on bad CSV data, no error handling. Security: file path written in CWD (directory traversal adjacent, low risk), CSV parsing accepts arbitrary input. Cross-promotion likely on missing types/tests and SRP violation.

assertions.text: Report flags meaningless function name `process` and/or parameter name `mode`
Report flags magic numbers (1.08, 1.15, 0.95, 90, 30) without explanation
Report flags positional tuple indexing (x[0]..x[4]) without documented schema
Report flags that process() violates single-responsibility by both transforming and writing a file
Report includes all three persona sections (Saboteur, New Hire, Security Auditor)
Final verdict is BLOCK or CONCERNS (not CLEAN)

evals.name: security-heavy-auth
evals.prompt:
Run an adversarial review on this file. It is a password reset endpoint just added to the auth service.

File: auth.js

Produce the full adversarial-reviewer output (all three personas, final verdict).
evals.expected_output: BLOCK verdict. Security Auditor dominates: (1) SQL injection via string interpolation into queries (email, user_id, token, hashed), (2) MD5 used for reset token — non-cryptographic and inputs are predictable (user_id + static salt + Date.now()), (3) MD5 used for password hashing (should be bcrypt/argon2), (4) hardcoded secret RESET_SECRET in source, (5) user enumeration via 404 vs 200 response, (6) reset token returned in response body (leaks token to any MITM / logs), (7) no token expiry / single-use enforcement, (8) PII (email) logged to console. Saboteur: crypto.createHash throws on undefined, no rate limiting, token not invalidated after use. New Hire: magic string `reset-salt-v1`, no tests, sparse comments. Cross-promotion expected on SQL injection and token handling.

assertions.text: Report flags SQL injection via string interpolation in at least one query
Report flags MD5 as unsuitable for reset tokens and/or password hashing
Report flags reset token being returned in the response body
Report flags user enumeration via differential 404 vs 200 response
Report includes all three persona sections (Saboteur, New Hire, Security Auditor)
Final verdict is BLOCK (has at least one CRITICAL finding)
